Getting to Know Your Local History

For anyone who wants to feel more rooted where they live. Each day is one small way to learn the stories of your street, town or city, from old buildings and street names to the people who came before.

Connection · Values · Loneliness · one to-do a day · you choose how many days

Start this challenge free

The first seven days

  • Day 1Step outside for a minute, say a quiet hello to your street, and notice one thing you like about it.
  • Day 2Think of one person who has lived near you longer than you have, and simply smile or wave next time you see them.
  • Day 3Look up your nearest public library's hours and see whether it has a local history room or collection.
  • Day 4Notice one small detail in your home today, like a light switch or a window latch, that hints at how old it is.
  • Day 5Tell a friend or family member one thing you love about the place where you live, old or new.
  • Day 6Look up how your street got its name, using your library's local history page or a free online search.
  • Day 7Ask an older neighbor what your street looked like when they first moved in.

Further into the year

The to-dos keep changing as the year goes on. A few from later in this theme:

  • Day 30Read a short picture book about your area's history with a child at bedtime.
  • Day 60Snap a picture of your main street from one spot on a crisp autumn morning to keep for the future.
  • Day 120Invite a friend to a free history event so you can go together.
  • Day 240Encourage a child to draw a picture of an old building you visited together.
  • Day 365Look back on the stories you've shared with others, and smile at how they now travel through your community.

How a challenge works

A Theraglee challenge is a theme with one small to-do for every day of a year. You choose how long yours runs, anywhere from a week to the full year, and each day you get the next to-do: something that takes a few minutes and fits inside an ordinary day. Tick it off when it is done. Nothing is scored and nothing is lost if you miss a day; the next to-do is simply waiting when you come back.

Challenges come with a free Theraglee account, which never asks for a card. Your progress stays private to you.
